medSchoolStudLife.diversity: The Sanford School of Medicine is committed to training a diverse group of students to meet the needs of the diverse population of the state.  Applicants may contact the Associate Dean for Community Health and Engagement for further information. In addition, we have a robust Academic Success program which includes one-on-one support with learning specialists, peer tutoring and student-led supplemental instruction sessions.
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: The Dean of Medical Student Affairs may grant an LOA for up to 1 year for medical or personal reasons.  Additional time is considered on a case-by-case basis for students in good standing pursuing educational opportunities.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: Many student organizations are active, with information available through the Student Affairs office.
medSchoolStudLife.setting: The first 3 semesters are based in Vermillion, SD. The clinical semesters (4-8) are largely based in either Sioux Falls, Yankton, or Rapid City.
medSchoolStudLife.housing: The vast majority of our students rent off-campus apartments/homes. More information provided during Interview Day sessions.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems:
Support is available. 

The University of South Dakota Sanford School of Medicine is committed to fostering a dynamic and welcoming learning environment for all. Therefore, the medical school is committed to both recruitment and retention of students, residents, faculty, and staff who through their intellectually and ideologically diverse perspectives enrich the learning environment. We provide equal opportunities for all. We value people with broad life experiences, with records of service to disadvantaged populations, and with other attributes that may enhance the learning community.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystemsForDisabilities:
Our core values of compassion and kindness permeates our interactions with all students, including those with disabilities. USD-SSOM endeavors to ensure accessibility and to create a respectful, accountable culture through our confidential disability support system. We encourage students with disabilities to disclose and seek accommodations. To learn more about accommodations at USD-SSOM please contact USD Disability Services at:

medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms:
Sanford School of Medicine Wellness Program: Our motto is "Well students, Well doctors, Well patients" 

Personal Wellness:
As a medical student, you have resources in place to help you overcome whatever you are going through. From Crisis lines to just someone to talk to, please reach out if you need help, all these services are confidential. These services are available for little to no cost to you as a student. 

Professional Wellness:
Medical Students deal with many concerns while pursuing their education. Things like academic concerns, anxiety, and career questions are common issues. The SSOM Chief Wellness Officer provides personal counseling and referrals when needed to a learning specialist, mental health counselors, etc. to help students work through these types of concerns. 

Wellness Committee:
The Sanford School of Medicine Medical Student Wellness program is based on a holistic model made up of programs that focus on the intellectual, environmental, emotional/spiritual, interpersonal, and physical well-being of the student throughout their medical education. A critical piece of the Sanford School of Medicine Wellness Program is the student-directed portion of the program. Wellness officers are elected for each class. These students oversee their budget and how they want to use it to promote wellness for each of their respective classes. Events/programs are intended to enable the students to incorporate these ideas to truly improve their well-being. Examples of activities students have planned in the past include yoga and other fitness classes; self-defense class; study-a-thons with snacks and massages; end of Year 1 picnic; movie night; and trivia Night.
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture: The USD Sanford School of Medicine (SSOM), with its award-winning curriculum and outstanding reputation in family medicine and rural medicine, prepares medical students for practice in all fields of medicine. Students receive a high-quality education strengthened by hands-on clinical experiences and our faculty's research. As South Dakota’s only medical school, the SSOM educates students across the entire state from our main campus locations in Vermillion, Sioux Falls, Yankton and Rapid City to our Frontier And Rural Medicine (FARM) Program sites in Chamberlain, Milbank, Mobridge, Parkston, Pierre, Spearfish, and Vermillion. Our school incorporates “kindness” into its programs and culture, identifying and elevating kindness as a fundamental component of healing and happiness. In addition, the SSOM values diversity in its many forms and persons with broad life experiences, records of service to disadvantaged populations, and with attributes that enhance the learning community.
medSchoolStudLife.transportationAdditionalInfo: Transportation services are generally available for students when scheduled class activities are at an alternate campus.

medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: Faculty are easily contacted.  Tutoring and Supplemental Instruction programs are available.
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: Starts during the first semester of year one.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: Combination of lecture, small group, team-based-learning, problem-based-learning, and clinical participation
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: Clinical rotations are taught in a Longitudinal Integrated Clerkship format and the core clerkships are during the Pillar 2 phase (4th and 5th semesters).
medSchoolCurriculum.lectureAttendance: Lecture attendance is optional with a few exceptions.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights: Semesters 1-3 (Pillar 1) are basic biomedical sciences taught primarily with an integrated organ system approach.  Semesters 4-5 (Pillar 2) are the core clinical rotations taught as longitudinal integrated clerkships.  Semesters 6-8 (Pillar 3) provide opportunities for electives, visiting student experiences, research or other personalized experiences to cap the student training for the MD.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: Students are exposed to primary care opportunities or rural medicine during all four years, plus there are primary care residencies in Family Medicine, Internal Medicine and Pediatrics in South Dakota.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms: Basic, clinical and translational research opportunities are available for interested students.  The school also has an MD/PhD dual degree program as well as a Scholarship Pathways Program with an opportunity for research as well as educational or service programs.
medSchoolCurriculum.academicSystemText: We have a 3 Pillar (Phase) curriculum. Our Pillar 1 pre-clerkship is approx. 17 months. Our Pillar 2 clerkship is approx. 12 months and our Pillar 3 curriculum is approx. 15 months.
medSchoolCurriculum.communityServiceText: A community based experience is required of all students.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchThesisText: Many research opportunities are available for students including an 8 week Summer Research Program prior to matriculation and a Scholarship Pathways Program that runs longitudinally over their 4 yrs.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation: The School of Medicine was established in 1907 as a 2-year school, and in 1974 became a 4-year, MD program graduating its first class in 1977.  Semesters 1-3 are based in Vermillion, Semesters 4-8 are in either Sioux Falls, Yankton or Rapid City with 13 students based in rural communities for their primary clinical training.  In 2005, the name was changed and is now University of South Dakota Sanford School of Medicine.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement:
The mission of the University of South Dakota Sanford School of Medicine is to provide the opportunity for South Dakota residents to receive a quality, broad-based medical education with an emphasis on family medicine.  The curriculum is to be established to encourage graduates to serve people living in the medically underserved areas of South Dakota and is to require excellence in the basic sciences and in all clinical disciplines.

The University of South Dakota Sanford School of Medicine is to provide to its students and to the people of South Dakota excellence in education, research and service.  To these ends, the School is to provide educational pathways leading to both the Doctor of Medicine and the Doctor of Philosophy Degrees. Quality health care for the people of South Dakota is addressed by undergraduate, graduate and continuing educational programs as well as by basic and applied medical research.  The Sanford School of Medicine should serve as a technical resource in the development of health care policy in the state and provide extension and research initiatives to improve the health care of the citizens of the state.

medSchoolApplication.amcasLettersText: Three individual recommendations, or evaluation materials/packet from a structured pre-medical committee with at least three contributing members on the pre-medical committee.
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance: Recommend at least one letter from a basic science faculty and if applicable, a research PI or mentor.
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay: Interview day will be virtual and consist of various presentations in the morning followed by one-on-one interviews in the afternoon. More information will be provided following interview invitation.
medSchoolApplication.interviewFormat: Currently, one on one virtual interviews. Please check for updates.
medSchoolApplication.secApplSentTo: Most SD residents and selected non-residents with strong ties to SD who have a cumulative GPA of at least 3.1 and a composite MCAT of at least 496.
medSchoolApplication.secApplLatestDtText: Due two weeks after receiving email request for secondary application.
medSchoolApplication.ctsRequired: For MD program: Non-residents with significant ties to South Dakota; Permanent residents of the US who have residency status in SD. For MD-PhD program: Open to all US citizens and permanent residents.
medSchoolApplication.acceptOutstateApplInformation: Need ties to state such as SD High School Grad, at least 90 credits at a SD college/university, parent living in SD, child of SSOM alumni, member of a federally recognized tribe from border state.
medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo:
**Response to COVID-19 - Information for the Admissions Cycle**Please note the following information about pass/fail requirements coursework, policies for online courses/labs and Letters of Evaluation:

Pass/Fail – The University of South Dakota Sanford School of Medicine (USD-SSOM) recognizes the impact of the COVID-19 outbreak in disrupting coursework. Although the committee would prefer grades for the prerequisite courses taken during the 2020 Spring/Summer/Fall semesters, we will accept Pass/Fail grades. 

Letters of Evaluation – As always, USD-SSOM accepts all letter types (Individual, letter packets or Committee letters)

Online Coursework and Labs -- As always, USD-SSOM accepts online coursework from any accredited institution.

Deposits are due two weeks after receiving an offer letter or notification of placement on our alternate list.

See the following URL: https://www.usd.edu/Admissions-and-Aid/Medical-School-Admissions/How-to-Apply
medSchoolApplication.gpaScreenAdditionalInfo: Minimum of a 3.1 undergraduate GPA but will consider graduate GPA also.
medSchoolApplication.minCreditHourInfo: Minimum of 24 credit hours and/or completion of graduate degree.
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: Courses taken at an accredited Community College will be considered.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo: We only accept grade updates from either the summer or fall semester of the application cycle. We do not accept any other updates or letters of intent.
medSchoolApplication.technicalStandardInfo: For Technical Standards please see our USD-SSOM Medical School Admissions how to apply webpage (Link below).

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid: Financial aid is administered through the office of Medical Student Affairs. Loans are available to medical students on the basis of demonstrated financial need. Scholarships are available to medical students on the basis of merit, mission and demonstrated financial need.
medSchoolFinancial.tuitionPolicy: Tuition is based on a per-semester rate independent of the number of credits taken.  Students must pay the tuition rate for each semester registered.

medSchoolAcceptance.waitlistProcedure: Applicants on Waitlist are ranked and offered a position in order of their rank.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec: Required courses should be at a level of the courses taken by a major in that field.  Courses that offer a lab are also recommended where possible.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: Applicants are chosen on the basis of intellect, character, and motivation. Their academic achievements as indicated by scholastic records and MCAT scores, and personal characteristics including integrity, work ethic, commitment to service, and other indicators of professional development are evaluated. Top priority for supplemental applications and interviews is given to legal residents of South Dakota, with invitation of selected non-residents with very strong ties to South Dakota, (which could also include non-residents who complete at least 90 credits at any four-year school in South Dakota for their bachelor's degree). An Alumni Student Scholars Program offers up to 4 future/provisional acceptances to South Dakota high school seniors.
